question: Outline the autocratic and laissez-faire styles of leadership.
markScheme:
Autocratic:
- Task oriented / dictator style / leader makes all the decisions / very direct in their approach
Laissez-faire:
- Provides little support or input / lets team members do as they wish
Accept other appropriate outlines.
Max 2 marks.

question: Explain when a coach would use the autocratic and laissez-faire styles in a sporting context.
markScheme:
Autocratic:
- Used when quick decisions need to be made / with large groups / when discipline is needed / with an inexperienced team / novices / cognitive learners / dangerous situations
Laissez-faire:
- Used when time is available / with experienced performers / autonomous learners / more motivated performers / no danger
Accept other appropriate explanations.
Max 2 marks.

question: Name and explain the stages of group formation and, using Chelladurai's and Fiedler's leadership models, explain how a leader can ensure a group work together to achieve success.
markScheme:
AO1 (4 marks): Stages of group formation: Forming, Storming, Norming, Performing, Adjourning/Mourning. Chelladurai's Model: depends on situational characteristics; leader's characteristics; group/member characteristics. Fiedler's Model: depends on the favourableness of the situation.
AO2 (5 marks): Forming - developing relationships / meeting new group members. Storming - individuals determine position within the group / conflict / establishing roles. Norming - co-operation / cohesion develops / common goal accepted. Performing - working to a common goal / cohesive team. Adjourning/Mourning - completing the task and breaking up the team. Chelladurai's Model: Situation - eg group size / nature of task / time available. Leadership - eg experience / personality / skill level. Members - eg motivation / ability / age. Fiedler's Model: favourableness depends on the task / leader's relationship with the group / leader's position of authority. Leadership style = task-orientated / autocratic or person-orientated / democratic.
AO3 (6 marks): Chelladurai's Model: if the required behaviour and the actual behaviour match the preferred behaviour, the group will work together / based on satisfaction leading to better performance. Fiedler's Model: use task-orientated in most/least favourable situations, eg a dangerous situation with novices. Use person-orientated in moderately favourable situations, eg new members joining a team for pre-season training.
Max 15 marks.

question: Which one of these is not a characteristic of a democratic leader?
markScheme:
Correct answer: A - Asks for little or no feedback.
1 mark for the correct option.
options: A - Asks for little or no feedback
B - Includes members of the group in decision making
C - May look for consensus via a vote
D - Values innovative ideas from others
correctOption: A - Asks for little or no feedback

question: Fiedler suggests that a task-orientated style of leadership should be used if the situation is classed as favourable. Using an example from volleyball, outline the characteristics of a favourable situation.
markScheme:
AO1 (sub max 2 marks):
- Leader respected by the group/leader has a good relationship with the group
- Clear task/goal/roles
- Good support network/high level of trust
- Group highly motivated/high ability/highly successful/good resources/equipment/facilities
AO2 (sub max 1 mark):
- For example, a respected volleyball coach whose squad are experienced, well resourced and focused on winning the league title for the third consecutive season
Accept other relevant responses. Answers must use an example.
Max 3 marks.

question: Leaders and coaches have an important role in developing the performance of their players. Outline the role of a cricket team captain and explain the difference between a prescribed leader and an emergent leader.
markScheme:
3 marks for 3 of:
A - (role of a leader) direct behaviour/influence others/motivate/set goals/provide guidance/provide feedback or equivalent
B - (prescribed leader) appointed by an external authority to lead the group, eg selected by the club committee
C - (emergent leader) appointed by/approved by the group (not just 'from within the team')
Max 3 marks.

question: The leader of a mountaineering expedition has an important role to ensure the team works together safely. Explain the term autocratic leader and outline when the autocratic style of leadership should be used.
markScheme:
3 marks for 3 of:
A - (Autocratic leader) makes all the decisions/no input from the team/task focused/not concerned about inter-personal relationships
B - (Situation) limited time available
C - (Situation) complex/dangerous task
D - (Situation) large number of people/performers
E - (Situation) clear/specific goals
F - (Situation) decisions need to be made quickly
G - (Situation) inexperienced group so need to be told what to do/experienced and willing to accept instructions (awarded if explained in correct context)
H - Most favourable/least favourable situations
(Sub max of 1 mark for explanation; sub max of 2 marks for situation)
Max 3 marks.

question: The figure below shows Chelladurai's multi-dimensional model of leadership. When quality of performance and levels of satisfaction are high, optimal levels of arousal are more likely. Use the figure above to explain how a coach can help a performer reach optimal levels of arousal.
markScheme:
Situation, performer and leader characteristics must be considered.
(Required behaviour) - determined by the situation
(Preferred behaviour) - the performer's ideal behaviour of the leader
(Actual leader behaviour) - the leader's action towards the performer
The closer the leader's behaviour is to that expected by the performer, the greater the chance of optimal arousal/performance will be of a high quality/levels of satisfaction
(Refers to the link between leader and group only, not the task.)
Having all three behaviours matching is the ideal.
Max 4 marks.

question: Fiedler suggested that the preferred style of leadership depends on the favourableness of the situation. Outline the characteristics of a favourable situation and name the style of leadership that should be used when this occurs.
markScheme:
4 marks for 4 of:
Task-centred/task-orientated/autocratic leadership style (sub max 1 mark)
Leader respected by group (NOT 'cohesiveness of the group')
Leader has a good relationship with the group
Group is highly motivated
Group has high ability/is highly successful
Clear task/goal/roles (NOT 'easy task')
Good support network
Good resources/equipment/facilities
Max 4 marks.

question: The captain of a team should be respected and should ensure that all players have a positive attitude. Identify three characteristics of a good leader and explain the difference between an emergent leader and a prescribed leader.
markScheme:
3 marks for 3 of: (take first 3 answers - if talking about leadership styles, this is NOT a characteristic)
Characteristics (any three from) confident/organised/inspirational/good communicator/knowledgeable/visionary/good decision maker/interpersonal skills/approachable/determined/empathy/charismatic/motivational/equivalent
Emergent leader - group approval/elected by the team
Prescribed leader - appointed by an external authority to lead the group
Max 3 marks.
